reason: Floral bracts are 'appressed hairy'. Hairy maps to pubescent hair (PATO_0001320) on the bract. 'Appressed' describes how the hairs lie and does not change the quality.

target: lemma (PO_0009037) villous, place: keel, proximal 1/3(–1/2) of length; degree sparse
fix: 'keel ... villous for 1/3 of length': the hairs sit on the lemma keel (its midvein ridge) only, so a place slot is needed. Do not use PO_0025327 keel, which is the legume keel petal.
reason: The flora says only the keel of the lemma is villous, and only along the lower third to half. 'Lemma villous' with no place reads as the whole lemma being hairy. The same sentence also allows 'infrequently glabrous'.

fix: In a count of veins, the whole that has them is the leaf blade (pattern 14 example: container PO_0020039), not 'vascular bundle', which is the parent class of vein.
reason: The count (4 or 5) and the 'each side of midrib' position are right. The whole that holds the lateral veins is set to vascular bundle (PO_0005020), which makes the count meaningless.

target: corolla lobe; colour green to whitish-green, with streaks/tips/margins brown, pink, magenta or violet
fix: In 'X with A, B or C streaks, tips or margins', the colours belong to streaks, tips or margins on a part whose main colour is X. Put them in a place slot (or striped colour pattern), not on the whole part.
reason: The corolla lobes are dull green to whitish-green. The brown, pink, magenta or violet colours are only on streaks, tips or margins. Saying the corolla is brown, pink, red or violet is false as it stands. Magenta as red is also loose.
'stem and branches subterete' = stem roughly terete. The 'approximately' qualifier is right.
'aril absent' = aril present, negated.
Stems 'strigulose or strigulose-pubescent': pilosity with a continuum from strigulose to pubescent fits the compound. The bearer is stem.
Petals 7–13 mm long.
Spikelets greenish or tinged purplish = green or purple, approximately.
'leaf blade ± lanceolate' = leaf lamina roughly lanceolate (its outline; the blade is pinnatisect).
In the leaf description, 'apex acuminate' is the tip of the leaf blade.

fix: 'Scalelike leaves ... 0.7–1.3 cm': the modifier 'scalelike' was dropped, so the measure went to the ordinary leaf. Map 'scalelike/scale leaves' to scale leaf (cataphyll).
reason: The 0.7–1.3 cm is the length of the scalelike leaves at the basal nodes. The ordinary leaves are described next and are different.

fix: In 'X including the ... sheath, which is ...', the 'which' clause describes the nearest noun (sheath), not the head noun (petiole).
reason: It is the broad striate sheath that is ± brownish, membranous and auriculate, not the petiole.

fix: 'tepals' must map to tepal (PO_0009033), never petal, especially in monocots like Allium.
reason: The flora says the tepals of Allium are erect or ± spreading. The position values are right.

fix: In a pinnate leaf description that runs on from 'leaflets ...', the shape, size and colour terms belong to the leaflet, not to the whole leaf.
reason: The sentence describes the leaflets ('terminal leaflet' follows). 'Subconcolorous' = roughly concolorous is right, but the flora adds that it applies when dried.

fix: 'above' after a hair term on a leaf or leaflet = adaxial surface (config/flora_context_words.tsv). It must fill the surface slot, here more than ever because 'beneath' gets another value.
reason: Only the upper surface is glabrous or sparingly pubescent. The lower surface is silky-pubescent, so without 'above' the statement is false for the leaflet.
Leaves whorled, about 4–6 at each node: a count of leaves per node. 'About' could also be kept as an 'approximately' qualifier.

fix: In 'one-seeded achene/fruit', the count belongs to the fruit. The fruit must fill the container slot (pattern 03), or the count reads as one seed per plant.
reason: The flora says each achene has one seed, not that the plant has one seed.
'étamines 10' = 10 stamens (per flower).
Moss leaf 'apex ... not cucullate' = leaf apex cucullate, negated. Leaf apex covers phyllid apex.

fix: In a list 'A, B or (rarely) C', all three values are alternatives. The pair extractor kept only the first two and dropped the rare third.
reason: The plant is erect, ascending or rarely decumbent. Recording only erect or ascending leaves out a state the flora names.
'Inflorescences pseudopaniculate' = inflorescence panicle-like (FLOPO_0991198).
Stamens alternate with the petals: alternate placement, with petal as the other part.

fix: 'glaucous' in floras means covered with a whitish waxy bloom: PATO_0104277, not the colour green or blue-green.
reason: 'Berries not glaucous' = fruit glaucous, negated. It says nothing about the fruit not being green.
The stipe of the sterile frond is dark purplish brown: stalk (stipe) brown, with the sterile frond as the whole. 'Dark purplish' only narrows the brown.
'Stems climbing, branched' = stem branched.
The epidermis of the petiole ± flakes off. FLOPO_0991021 exfoliating covers a plant axis whose surface tissue flakes, and the 'approximately' qualifier fits.
Leaves 3–5.5 × 2–3 cm: the first number is the length of the blade.

target: leaf margin teeth (tip ending in a bristle)
fix: 'bristle-tipped' describes the tip of the part just named (here the leaf teeth). It must not create an awn: PO_0025349 is the awn of a grass glume, lemma or palea.
reason: The teeth of the Heuchera leaf lobes are mucronate and bristle-tipped. A Heuchera has no awns, so 'awn present' is false.
'filets des étamines rouges' = filaments red.
